questions.question: Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Savita will deliver a speech on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Savita will deliver a speech on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti.

options.text: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is being delivered by Savita.
options.html: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is being delivered by Savita.

options.text: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech was delivered by Savita.
options.html: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech was delivered by Savita.

options.text: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech will be delivered by Savita.
options.html: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech will be delivered by Savita.

options.text: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is to be delivered by Savita.
options.html: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is to be delivered by Savita.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech will be delivered by Savita'.

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice and 'Savita' is the subject and ''on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti'' is the object.
  • When we convert this sentence into a passive voice, the subject 'Savita' of the active voice becomes the object, the object ''on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti''becomes the subject.
  • The passive format "'will + be + V3 (delivered)" should be used.
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the future simple tense.


Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual

questions.question: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. How many languages do you learn at school?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

How many languages do you learn at school?

options.text: How many languages will you learn at school?
options.html: How many languages will you learn at school?

options.text: Languages are learnt by how many at school?
options.html: Languages are learnt by how many at school?

options.text: How many languages are learnt by you at school?
options.html: How many languages are learnt by you at school?

options.text: How many languages have you being learnt by you learning at school?
options.html: How many languages have you being learnt by you learning at school?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'How many languages are learnt by you at school?'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
  • The process of transformation is as follows:
    • In 'active-passive' transformation except for (who and whom) rest of the Wh-family Pronouns will remain unchanged.  
    • Here in the given question 'How many languages' will remain unchanged.
    • 'do learn' will be changed into 'are learnt'. 
    • Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be added. 
       

Correct Sentence: How many languages are learnt by you at school?

Hinglish

  •  दिया गया वाक्य Active Voice का उदाहरण है। दिए गए प्रश्न के अनुसार हमें इसे Passive Voice में बदलना है।
  • परिवर्तन की प्रक्रिया इस प्रकार है:
    • 'Active-Passive' परिवर्तन में (who और whom) को छोड़कर शेष Wh- परिवार pronouns अपरिवर्तित रहेंगे।
    • यहां, दिए गए प्रश्न में 'How many languages' अपरिवर्तित रहेंगी।
    • 'do learnt' को 'are learnt' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
    • अंत में, preposition 'by' जोड़ा जाएगा।

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The school will hire new teachers.

  • Option 3: "New teachers are hired by the school." – This is present tense, not future tense.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The company will release the new product next month.

The correct answer is: The new product will be released by the company next month.

Key Points

  • The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.
  • The usage of a helping verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.
  • The preposition “by” is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.
  • The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.
  • The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.
  • Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + made + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).
  • For example:
    • He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)
    • The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

questions.solution:

Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "The team will announce the winner tomorrow."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the winner" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "will announce" to "will be announced" (future simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the team."
  • Ensure the time phrase "tomorrow" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "The team will announce tomorrow the winner." – This is not in passive voice.
  • Option 2: "The winner will announce tomorrow by the team." – Incorrect structure.
  • Option 4: "Tomorrow will be announced the winner by the team." – Incorrect structure.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They were preparing banners with different designs for the sports meet.
questions.questionHtml:

options.html: Banners were prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. 'Banners were being prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the active voice. We have to change the sentence into passive form. 
  • The given sentence is written in 'past continuous tense.'
  • The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
    • Active Voice: Subject + was/were + (verb+ing) + Object.
    • Passive Voice:  Object + was/were + being + V3 + by (preposition) + Subject.
  • Let’s see another example:
    • Active voice: They were organising the party.
    • Passive voice: The party was being organised by them.
  • The subject of the given sentence is 'They' and the object of the given sentence is 'banners'. 
  • The subject 'They' will be changed into 'them'.
  • So, in the passive voice, the position of ‘subject’ and ‘object’ will be interchanged and 'by' will be added. 
  • Also here, 'were preparing' will be changed into 'were being prepared'.
  • The remaining portion will not be changed. 

 

Correct Sentence: Banners were being prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 

Key Points

  • The active sentence “He has written a best-selling novel” is in the present perfect tense (has written). 
  • When converting to the passive voice, the tense remains the same:
  • has written → has been written

So, the correct passive construction is: A best-selling novel has been written by him.

Additional Information

Why others are incorrect:

  • Option 1: was being written → past continuous (wrong tense)
  • Option 3: was written → simple past (tense changes)
  • Option 4: would have been written → conditional perfect (changes meaning)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
